d: Explore how to find and import audio assets for use in your games.
h:
You can find a wide variety of free‑to‑use audio assets in the Creator Store, or you can import audio assets that you're certain you have permission to use, such as audio that you make yourself. The asset privacy system automatically ensures that the IDs of your imported audio can't be accessed by users without proper permissions.

Find audio

The Creator Store tab of the Toolbox contains a wide variety of free-to-use audio assets made by Roblox and the Roblox community for creators to use within their games, including more than 100,000 professionally-produced sound effects and music tracks from top audio and music partners.

To find audio assets on the Creator Store:

  1. In the Toolbox, navigate to the Creator Store tab, then use the category selector dropdown to select Audio.

  1. Use the keyword search, quick filter options, and/or advanced filters to narrow down the results.

  1. Right-click any audio asset, then select Copy Asset ID to copy the asset ID to your clipboard. You can now paste this asset ID into a AudioPlayer object to play the audio.

If you click any audio asset, Studio inserts it as a new Sound instance into the Explorer window. However, Sound objects don't have the same dynamic functionality as AudioPlayer objects.

Import audio

You can import custom audio through the Asset Manager, Creator Dashboard, and Open Cloud API as long as your audio meets the following requirements:

  • You have the legal rights to that audio asset.
  • It adheres to the Community Rules and Terms of Use.
  • It's a single track/stream in either .mp3, .ogg, .wav or .flac format.
  • It's less than 20 MB in size and 7 minutes in duration.
  • Its sample rate is less than or equal to 48 kHz.
  • Its channels are set to mono or stereo 2.0, 3.0, or 5.1 surround.

If you're ID verified, you can import 2,000 free audio assets per 30 days; if you're unverified, you can import 100 free audio assets per 30 days. If a daily import limit exists, it's removed and replaced with a simplified monthly limit.

Studio assigns each new audio asset a unique asset ID that you can use within your games to play the audio.

To import audio through the Asset Manager:

  1. Click the Import button.
  2. Select and then confirm the audio files you want to import from your local system.
  3. Once you confirm the imports and the files import successfully, they display with a green checkmark and a completed status.

To standardize the playback format and check for corrupt or invalid files, Studio transcodes imported audio before saving it as an asset. If you receive an error while importing audio, Studio is likely rejecting it during the transcode process. In addition, some older audio tools generate invalid file headers or frames when exporting.

If Studio continues to reject the audio you're trying to import, ensure your audio tools are updated, then verify that the audio files meet the import requirements.

To import audio through the Creator Dashboard:

  1. In the horizontal navigation, select Development Items. All assets you have previously imported display within their respective category.
  2. In the sub-horizontal navigation, select Audio.
  3. Click the Upload Asset button. The Upload Asset page displays.
  4. In the Upload Asset page,
  5. Click the Upload button, then select and then confirm the audio file you want to import from your local system.
  6. Fill out the Name and Description fields with the audio file's relevant information.
  7. At the bottom of the page, click the Upload button.

Your audio assets are now within the moderation queue and are only visible to you within the Audio tab of the Creator Dashboard's Development Items page.

To import audio through an HTTP request:

  1. Copy the API key to the x-api-key request header of the Create Asset endpoint.

  2. In your request:

  3. Specify that the target asset type is Audio.

  4. Add your audio asset's name and description.
  5. Add the creator information.
    • If you want to create the audio asset on your own behalf, add your user ID. You can find your user ID on the URL of your Roblox profile. For example, for https://www.roblox.com/users/1234567/profile, your user ID is 1234567.
    • If you want to create the audio asset as a group asset, add the group ID of your group. You can find the group ID on the URL of your group's page. For example, for https://www.roblox.com/groups/7654321/example-group#!/, the group ID is 7654321.
  6. Add the file path and content type of your asset.

```bash curl --location 'https://apis.roblox.com/assets/v1/assets' \ --header 'x-api-key: ${ApiKey}' \ --form 'request="{ \"assetType\": \"Audio\", \"displayName\": \"Name\", \"description\": \"This is a description\", \"creationContext\": { \"creator\": { \"userId\": \"${userId}\" # Use groupId for creating a group asset } } }"' \ --form 'fileContent=@"/filepath/audio.mp3";type=audio/mpeg'

```

After the audio assets pass moderation, you can reuse them in any project on the platform. Although you are initially the only one who can view and use private audio assets, the asset privacy system lets you grant usage permissions to specific friends and experiences.

Visibility

When you upload audio to Roblox, it is automatically classified as a sound effect or a song. Sound effects are not eligible to appear on the details page of the game in which they're used, but they can be distributed on the Creator Store. A song can appear on the game details page if:

  • It passes all moderation and copyright checks.
  • It meets the minimum duration, playback (number of unique plays), and platform age requirements.
  • It has a meaningful and appropriate title.
  • The uploader is ID verified.
  • The uploader has acknowledged the Roblox Audio Terms of Use.

Eligible songs will become visible on the game details page by default when the above requirements are met. You can toggle this visibility on the asset's Configure page in the Creator Hub. You can also add the Roblox usernames of song composers and collaborators in the Song Artist field; if this field is left blank, you'll be listed as the artist.

Once a song is on the game details page, players can click the song tile to see the song details page. Here, they can view additional information about the track and listen to a 15-second preview.

kid.simple: This page shows you where to get sounds for your game and how to upload your own. You can grab free sounds from the Creator Store in Studio's Toolbox, or upload audio files you made yourself. Every sound gets an asset ID, which is the number your game uses to play it. It also explains the rules your files must follow and how songs can show up on your game's page.
kid.analogy: Uploading audio is like turning in a library book: the library checks it, gives it a code number, and after that anyone with permission can find it by that number.
keyPoints: To find free sounds, open the Toolbox, go to the Creator Store tab, and pick Audio from the category dropdown.
Use search and filters to narrow results, then right-click a sound and choose Copy Asset ID.
Paste that asset ID into an `AudioPlayer` to play the sound.
Clicking a sound in the Toolbox inserts an older `Sound` object, which cannot do as much as an `AudioPlayer`.
You can upload your own audio through the Asset Manager, the Creator Dashboard, or the Open Cloud API.
Uploaded files must be yours to use, follow the Community Rules, be `.mp3`, `.ogg`, `.wav`, or `.flac`, be under 20 MB and under 7 minutes.
ID-verified creators can upload 2,000 free audio files every 30 days; unverified creators can upload 100.
New uploads go through moderation first, and at the start only you can use them unless you share permission.

terms.Toolbox: A Studio window where you can browse and insert free models, images, sounds, and more.
terms.Asset Manager: A Studio window that lists the files (assets) in your project and lets you import new ones.
terms.Creator Dashboard: The website at create.roblox.com where you manage your games and uploaded files.
terms.Open Cloud API: A way for programs outside Roblox to talk to Roblox, for example to upload files automatically. Most beginners will not need it.
terms.moderation: Roblox checking your upload to make sure it follows the rules before others can hear it.
terms.transcode: Roblox converts your file into its own standard sound format when you upload it. Broken files fail at this step.
terms.sample rate: How many tiny slices of sound are recorded each second. Roblox accepts up to 48 kHz, which means 48,000 slices per second.
terms.mono / stereo: Mono is one sound channel. Stereo is two channels (left and right). Roblox also accepts 3.0 and 5.1 surround.
terms.asset privacy: A system that keeps your uploaded audio private to you until you give other people or games permission to use it.
terms.ID verified: Your Roblox account has been confirmed with an official ID, which unlocks higher upload limits.
terms.sound effect vs. song: Roblox sorts each upload as one or the other. Only songs can appear on your game's details page.

watchOut: Clicking a sound in the Toolbox drops in a `Sound` object. If you want the newer system, right-click and copy the asset ID instead, then paste it into an `AudioPlayer`.
If your upload fails, the file may be broken or too big. Check it is under 20 MB, under 7 minutes, and in a supported format.
Your freshly uploaded sound will not play for others until it passes moderation, so upload early.
Only upload sounds you made or have the rights to. Copying music from elsewhere can get it removed.
